parsed.explanation: Combined regime rated as one system. Documented national exposures dominate: passports with sex markers restricted and some travellers' documents confiscated or blocked, leaving some stranded; entry cables that refuse mismatched or doubted sex and allow a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding; birth-sex or conversion-style custody policy with documented beatings and sexual abuse in immigration custody; and official framing of trans-aligned groups as a counterterrorism priority. The division adds no criminal offence and no facility-law enforcement, and recognises same-sex marriage, but its marker rules are tightening and its own protections are patchy. Care and sports restrictions are unresolved. Visitor risk is high, not severe, because the documented harms are at the border and in custody.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport sex markers restricted to sex at birth; new applications processed as M or F; passports confiscated or blocked, leaving travellers stranded. Entry cable refuses on any document discrepancy or doubt about sex; possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; a civil-liberties suit is pending and some measures are enjoined or unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor's home passport governs entry; a mismatch triggers refusal, and the national regime applies regardless of division rules.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Corrections bureau adopted conversion-style policies (hair cut, hormone removal) with reported denial of care; the bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner counts. Immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Earlier LGBTQ prison orders rescinded; no documented remedy operating.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document doubt at entry can lead to detention, and national custody policy then applies to the detainee.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National government-funded facilities restricted by birth sex. Four states criminalise bathroom use in some circumstances, including a documented trespass arrest; this division is not one of them. Division facility law covers K-12 and colleges, public and private, with birth-certificate designation and no penalty.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division facility law has no enforcement mechanism; no documented case brought under it. Single-occupancy exemption.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility rules at national and division level stack; a visitor's itinerary through other states can meet criminal bathroom rules.

care_services.exposure: National subpoenas of hospital records for patients under 19; proposed federal rule to bar public insurance for minors' care (not in force). Division bans under-18 puberty blockers, hormones and surgery, but the bill's operative status is unresolved after appellate re-injunction.
care_services.protection: Emergency care not documented as barred by gender; adult care rules proposed in 2024 were withdrawn and are not in force.
care_services.interaction: Medication or care needs of a visitor could meet the national records regime or a division ban depending on status.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official hostility: a national counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for priority neutralisation; a reward system for arrests; an executive order directing criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Statement that counterterrorism powers will not target people who merely disagree.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National framing reaches visitors through policing and entry screening; the division has no comparable framing in its documents.

minors_guardians.exposure: Family with a minor faces national threats of prosecution for facilitating social transition, school outing requirements in the division (residents), and the risk that a minor's records are subpoenaed. A minor at a school or college is subject to birth-certificate-based facility rules.
minors_guardians.protection: Division has no criminal offence for a guardian; the facility law has no enforcement mechanism.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's documents, school exposure and guardian's presentation can all meet national prosecution threats and division school rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National bias statistics show sexual-orientation bias dominates reported hate incidents; gender-identity hate-crime coverage is partial, with 37 states lacking anti-bias statutes as of 2019. Division has no state anti-discrimination statute for gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 33 cities and counties ban gender-identity discrimination; a civil-rights reading of Title VII-type law applies; a visible arrest for the trespass offence was reported as the first in its state.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local ordinances cover only some localities; a visitor in an uncovered area has only national recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division marker rules tightening: August 2026 announcement limits markers to M or F with exact-matching birth certificate or passport; some counties refuse birth-certificate corrections. Trans candidates disqualified under a disclosure law.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Marriage recognised regardless of sex; court-order and physician-declaration path for licence changes; X option since 2022; birth-certificate corrections permitted since 2021 in most counties.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: The exact-match rule links the division's document regime to the national passport regime, which applies to all travellers.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in the universal birth-sex exclusion from public facilities and emergency ward placement, with complaints rejected. This case is lower because it adds documented border refusals and stranding, documented custody abuse, and official framing of trans groups as security targets. It is higher because the division has no presentation or facility criminal penalty.

Lower than the anchor for the presence of documented state-led custody abuse and border refusals, which are comparable in severity. This case is higher because it lacks a presentation offence, police extortion and passport confiscation at local transit, and its division enforcement is absent.

Lower because the anchor covers a single security-screening search regime with complaints acknowledged and some remedies. This case adds national custody abuse, nationwide passport blocking and a national threat-framing posture, so it sits below the elevated band.

parsed.synthesis: The national border and custody regime is the primary exposure. A visitor whose home passport conflicts with appearance is refused at entry, may face a fraud-ineligibility finding, and cannot rely on division rules to offset that. Documented custody abuse in immigration detention is severe and reaches visitors. The division adds no criminal offence and no facility enforcement, and marriage recognition helps couples, but its exact-match marker rule and unresolved care ban add uncertainty. Pending litigation means the exposure depends on what is in effect at the time of travel.
